issues.problem: The plan is dated against a window that has already closed or is about to. Today is Oct 7: the Aug 22 Chuck Brown Day seed and most of Hispanic Heritage Month are gone, Howard Homecoming is days to weeks away, and the Oct 30 Cup Night is 23 days out. A co-created go-go capsule (band contracts, Chuck Brown estate and MICA Globe permissions, original wood-type alphabet, lab-dipped neon inks) cannot be designed, cleared, produced and shipped in that time.
issues.fix: Re-baseline the calendar to what is real. For Oct 30 use only product already in the pipeline (Dybantsa and Young name-and-number, Wards & Codes if it is already tooled). Announce the go-go partnership at Oct 30 as a credited commitment and re-time the first drop to the February official-music anniversary or Go-Go Month in May, with Chuck Brown Day Aug 2027 as the true seed.

issues.problem: Oct 30 carries five launches at once (Dybantsa, Tonight Only, Eight Wards, a 7th Street pop-up and a mambo-sauce carryout) and is called the era's first 'national-scale' home moment. It is a Friday Cup group game against Charlotte, with no national window, and the Wizards host only two of the four Cup Fridays through Nov 27. 'Weekly Cup Friday drops' therefore do not match the home schedule, and the Nov 24-25 Cup Nights may not include Washington.
issues.fix: Pick one hero for Oct 30, and make it the Wards & Codes civic capsule or the Dybantsa name-and-number moment, not both plus go-go. Tie Cup drops to the actual home dates and stage the rest behind the first-month sell-through gate.

issues.problem: A City Edition revival is a November-to-April product, but the brief times blossom product to late March. Pink product launched with the uniform in the Nov-Dec gifting window will sit four months before the tourist peak, while product held for March misses the uniform's launch spike. The brief also says the blossom is the tourist side of the line and that visitors do not buy NBA gear, yet it ranks Late Bloom a high-size priority and adds a tourist cap.
issues.fix: Split the plan in two. At the City Edition launch, sell the uniform and one local-first piece (Kwanzan pink and Hains Point, not the Mall). In March-April add only a small tourist-price souvenir tier through the arena and Georgetown, and treat Late Bloom as medium size. Keep the dependency explicit: the revival is a single report.

issues.problem: The go-go uniform is built for 'the next new City slot', which is 2027-28 at the earliest, since 2026-27 is reportedly the blossom revival. It is not an actionable 2026-27 item, yet it drives the headline thesis, opportunity 1 and the Oct 30 story. The design also leans on fluorescent split-fountain panels, a hem-to-armpit gradient, a roto-tom emboss and a live pocket band, none of which is checked against NBA uniform rules on color, contrast and manufacturing.
issues.fix: Reframe The Pocket as a 2027-28 concept brief with a 12 to 18 month partner timeline. Prove it first on non-uniform product (warm-ups, shooting shirts, court graphics) in 2026-27, and check the neon palette with Nike's NBA uniform team before the partners see it.

issues.problem: The go-go plan is the right call but still has extractive edges. 'Cowbell zipper pull', the roto-tom emboss and 'PA Tape' turn instruments and a recording practice into trim. A revenue share to 'youth music programs' is unnamed. Naming the Globe poster style invites the question of who owns the archive. Go-go is Black DC's music and the plan depends on a few well-known bands and organizers to speak for it.
issues.fix: Put the terms in the brief: a named paid creative lead from the poster community, band fees plus royalty, a fixed percentage to a named go-go youth program, and veto power for Don't Mute DC on the final graphics. Keep the instruments off the product as decoration and credit the poster artist by name on the hangtag.

issues.problem: The moombahton '108' shirt credits Dave Nada, a DJ who is not Salvadoran-American, as the origin story. That centers the credit on the producer rather than on the Salvadoran and Latino community whose party scene in Maryland and Northern Virginia the sound grew from. The window (Sept 15-Oct 15) is also mostly over, and Fiesta DC and Hispanic Heritage Month are themselves a tight slot.
issues.fix: Lead credit with Salvadoran-American designers and DJs from Langley Park and Columbia Heights and treat Nada as one named contributor. Move to a spring or summer slot with a named local partner and a clear payment plan, or drop it if there is no partner by December.

issues.problem: The 17th Street High Heel Race is a Dupont Circle event with its own audience, while the Center for Black Equity runs DC Black Pride. The plan treats them as one partnership and gives CBE approval over a product tied to a different community's event, three days before a game. A Pride-colored warm-up also has no tie to the team or to the Wizards fan base.
issues.fix: Decide which community this is for. If it is Black Pride, run it in May with CBE and Black LGBTQ+ DC designers and tie it to the Mystics. If it is Dupont, work with that event's organizers, or drop the Oct 27 slot.

issues.problem: The brief says restraint is part of the design brief, but the lead civic product is the 'Justitia Omnibus' hoodie with motto neck tape. The motto and flag are the statehood and home-rule movement's own symbols, and the 2025 federal police takeover, the shutdown and job cuts make them harder to read as neutral in fall 2026. The risk is higher because the commuter capsule below targets the federal workers this same section says are hurt.
issues.fix: Keep the flag as an identity mark and drop the motto from product unless a DC-based partner co-signs it. Make 'check local sentiment before each civic drop' a named owner and date, and take federal-worker framing out of the commuter capsule.

issues.problem: A packable navy coaches jacket, a waffle quarter-zip, a heather-gray fleece and a tonal cap would work for any city with a subway. Only the fare-card sleeve is DC, and it needs WMATA/SmarTrip clearance. This capsule is also not grounded in any single dossier insight beyond 'commuters exist'.
issues.fix: Cut it, or fold the fare-card sleeve and one office-to-arena colorway into the core Wards & Codes range. If kept, ground it in a specific local ritual (Gallery Place-Chinatown gameday transfer, Metro Center) and clear WMATA before design lock.

issues.problem: A blue-crab gradient and R-month oysters read as Maryland and Chesapeake more than the District, and Baltimore and Under Armour own that territory. Only the Maine Avenue Fish Market tie is DC. A navy-to-red gradient fleece is a color story with a crab label on it.
issues.fix: Drop Steamed from the uniform alternates. If food is wanted, use mambo sauce, half-smokes and Ben's Chili Bowl (license needed), which the swap test confirms are DC.

issues.problem: The 'Pivot' lifestyle hoops shoe with a suede pivot circle is not tied to any insight and is a footwear brief inside an apparel strategy. The Goodman League licensing assumes organizers control the marks and a venue that has changed with Barry Farm's redevelopment. Mystics product assumes a 2027 relationship the dossiers did not confirm.
issues.fix: Remove the shoe. Keep the Goodman kit and the Ward 8 women's hoops shooting shirt, with a signed agreement and a fee before any announcement. Verify the 2027 Goodman venue and the Mystics' status first.

issues.problem: Swap the city name and the Dybantsa plan still works: a No. 1 pick, name-and-number jerseys, youth tees and an aglet pack. He is not from the DMV and the brief offers no local story for him. The 'Mambo' orange drawcord pack puts a Black DC food brand on a colorway, which is closer to a gimmick than a collaboration.
issues.fix: Give him a DC hook the dossiers can support: a local high-school or Goodman court appearance, a ward-and-county graphic made with his teammates, or a Ward 8 youth clinic at CareFirst Arena. Either make the sauce partnership a real co-brand or remove the aglet pack.

issues.problem: The food and culture dossiers name DC's diaspora corridors (Ethiopian Shaw and Silver Spring, Vietnamese Eden Center, Salvadoran Columbia Heights and Langley Park) and flag the sacred and political imagery to avoid. The brief uses only the Salvadoran '108' idea. The roster has Alex Sarr and a No. 1 pick with African roots (verify heritage before saying anything public), and DC has one of the largest Ethiopian communities outside Africa.
issues.fix: Add one diaspora lane with a named community partner and a payment plan, such as an Ethiopian-American designer-led capsule or a Little Ethiopia gameday partnership, with no flags, crosses or national symbols. Run it by the culture dossier's avoid list.

issues.problem: Nike's own DC assets are underused. The brief lists Georgetown as a licensing risk when the school is a Jordan Brand program, and the ties to Team Takeover, Mystics and Kiki Rice stop at one line in the insights. The DMV scholastic scene (WCAC, Paul VI, DeMatha, Gonzaga, Bishop O'Connell) is where DMV fans claim players, but it appears only as a February warm-up.
issues.fix: Make the Nike family the spine of the Ward 8 and hoops plan: a Jordan Brand and Georgetown heritage piece, a Team Takeover and WCAC school-colors capsule, and Kiki Rice in a Mystics story. Check the Georgetown and Howard apparel deals before naming either.

issues.problem: 'Wizards Arcade' black-and-bronze and MAGFest (held in Maryland) is a niche tie-in to the Jordan-era look that the uniform dossier calls polarizing. 'Faded royal' for 1978 may not match the Bullets team's actual colors. The Bullets name is still a gun-violence issue and needs team sign-off.
issues.fix: Merge into one Bullets-era classic with the team's approval (red, white and blue stripes, Unseld and Hayes-era numerals) and drop the arcade idea unless there is local gaming-community evidence. Check 1978 colors against archive images.

issues.problem: A licensed Howard capsule with student designers and a WHUR 'Quiet Storm' velour set cannot clear licensing and production by mid-to-late October. A velour set has no link to basketball or the Wizards. It also lands the same week as the Dybantsa and Oct 30 launches.
issues.fix: Treat Homecoming 2026 as a relationship-building presence only (credited student designers, no product) and plan the licensed capsule for Homecoming 2027. Keep velour out unless WHUR co-signs and the story is the team's.

issues.problem: Fandom is scored 44 and retail 58 while the playbook assumes four themes, eight opportunities and a three-tier ladder across PG, NoVA and the District. That is more than a hedged, health-dependent roster can support, and it leaves out the first buy sizing.
issues.fix: Cut to three priorities (Wards & Codes, Dybantsa/Young core, the go-go partnership build). Put the other items in a 'later' tier with the gates the brief already describes.

issues.problem: The brief's December plan includes a 'Steamed' fleece launch and a contingency for a Cup quarterfinal. Quarterfinals are Dec 4-5 and go to the higher seeds' homes, which Washington is unlikely to be given its group (Boston, Atlanta, Charlotte, Chicago, with the Celtics seeded higher). The Dec 11 final is in Indianapolis, so there is no DC Cup event to plan around.
issues.fix: Delete the Cup quarterfinal contingency, or keep it as a one-line reserve with no product commitment. Spend December on gifting and the area-code and ward range.

strengths: The thesis is right and specific: DC civic type, the flag, wards and area codes outsell the Wizards wordmark, and no other market can claim that system.
Treating go-go as a paid, credited co-creation and launching it in Shaw or Anacostia before downtown shows real respect for who owns the culture.
The Ward 8 corridor (CareFirst Arena, Goodman League, the Go-Go Museum & Cafe) is a local finding that passes the swap and insider tests.
The risk section is honest about adidas and Under Armour, the Bullets name, the licensing minefield and a volatile roster, and the 'no crew names, no gun wordplay' rules are good.
The staged-replenishment approach and the three-ring view (District, PG County, NoVA) fit a 17-65 team with a health-dependent core.
summary: The brief is stronger on culture than on calendar. Its core ideas (civic type, Wards & Codes, a co-created go-go story, Ward 8) are specific, respectful and DC-only, but it is written as if there were months to launch and it stacks too much on Oct 30, a Friday Cup game against Charlotte. Four things need fixing first: re-baseline the go-go and Howard items to 2027 realities, split the City Edition blossom plan into a November and a spring release, replace the generic and Maryland-flavored pieces (commuter layer, crab, shoe), and add a diaspora and Nike-family lane that the dossiers support. Overall: sound strategy with weak timing and some padding, medium confidence.
